cards.text: Paul is closing out his letter to the believers in Thessalonica, and he saves something serious for the end. He gives them a command, and he gives it in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. When Paul pulls out THAT name, friend, you put the cookie down and listen.

cards.question: Paul commands the brothers to keep away from any brother who does what?
Paul reminds them to imitate how he and his team lived among them. True or false: back then, his team ate people's food without paying for it.

cards.text: Nope, they worked in labor and toil, NIGHT and DAY. I pulled night-and-day shifts for years in a junk drawer too, friend, except my whole job was collecting dust.

cards.question: Paul's team worked night and day so they wouldn't be a ___ to any of them.
Paul says his team did have the right to be supported by the believers. So why work night and day anyway?

answers.text: To be an example to imitate
To prove they were the strongest
To save up for the next trip

cards.question: Even while Paul was with them, he gave them a rule about work. What was it?

answers.text: Anyone unwilling to work shall not eat
Anyone who works shall rest each week
Anyone who eats shall share with others

cards.question: Paul has heard news. Some of them are living undisciplined lives, accomplishing nothing but being ___.

cards.text: Busy doing nothing and busy in everybody else's business, like the coworker with zero tasks and FORTY opinions about yours. So Paul speaks right to them, by our Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.question: Paul commands and urges them to begin working ___ to earn their own living.
Then Paul turns to the brothers who have been doing right all along. What does he tell them?

cards.text: As for anyone who won't obey what this letter says, Paul tells the church to take note of him and not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed.

cards.question: Paul doesn't want stepping back from that person to be the end of it. How should the church see him?

cards.text: That's family, friend. You can be completely fed up with family and STILL save them the last cookie.

cards.question: Paul closes with a blessing. True or false: he prays that the Lord of peace would give them peace only in hard times.

cards.text: After praying that the Lord would be with all of them, Paul picks up the pen himself. The last note I wrote, I held the pencil with my mustache, so I RESPECT a man doing his own lettering.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says writing the greeting in his own hand is his mark in every letter.

cards.text: Out of every word he could end on, Paul picks grace: "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you." Now THAT is how you seal a box.

findings.problem: The setup line 'Paul reminds them to imitate how he and his team lived among them' gives away the answer to card 6, which asks why the team worked night and day ('To be an example to imitate', 3:9).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question calls Paul's command 'a rule about work.' The text calls it a command: 'we gave you this command' (3:10).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to guess the word 'busybodies.' Nothing earlier sets it up. 'Daydreamers' and 'spectators' fit 'accomplishing nothing' just as well, so the right pick depends on knowing the wording, not on reasoning about the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'The brothers who have been doing right all along' adds a time span the text doesn't give. Verse 13 says only 'But as for you, brothers.'

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Don't grow weary in well-doing,' uses Bible-sounding wording ('well-doing'). The wrong answers use plain modern wording, so the right one stands out. The setup's 'doing right' also points toward 'well-doing.'

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'As a stranger to ignore' sits close to 3:14, which says 'Do not associate with him.' A baker could argue it is partly true within the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: This story card only reacts to card 13's answer. It tells no new part of the passage and does not move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: 'He prays that the Lord of peace would give them peace' calls the blessing a prayer. The text says 'Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace' (3:16). This is the same pattern as the Naomi example.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: 'After praying that the Lord would be with all of them' calls the blessing a prayer. The text says 'The Lord be with all of you' (3:16).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
